note:
201/9's OWED PAIRED RE-FLIGHT OF THE PROBE GATE, which came back with a different answer than the one it was sent for. The handoff row asked for the difference between what the `noprobe` ablation SAID (1.6 ms, the sweep) and what the demand gate actually REMOVED. The answer is that it removed nothing on this surface, because nothing was running: `apps/dispatch` never assigns `Engine.probeCenter` (only `apps/web` and `apps/engine-lab` do), so `scheduleProbe` has returned at its FIRST condition on every console capture ever taken. The env probe has never rendered a face here. That makes `?ablate=probe` a NULL ARM on this surface -- `field` and `noprobe` differ by one array store (`frameData[91] = 0`) and one counter tick, and the shipped bundle was read byte-for-byte to confirm it.

So the five windows below are not an A/B. They are the same frame flown five times, and what they measure is THE INSTRUMENT. They span 18.11 to 20.58 ms -- 2.47 ms peak to peak -- with the two `noprobe` windows sitting INSIDE the `field` windows' own range. The first three flights read field 20.17, noprobe 18.40, field 20.58 and looked like a clean, thermally-bracketed 2 ms effect; the fifth flight is the one that broke it, because it is a `field` window at 18.11.

WHAT THIS COSTS THE RECORD. `render/ablation.ts` claims ~450 moving frames give 'roughly half a millisecond of resolution'. On this device, on this route, a null arm reads 2.47 ms. Every arm in the 09-05 sweep under that number is inside the noise and may not be cited as a cost: `noprobe` 1.6, `nocloud` 1.8, `noskylut` 1.0, `bloom4` 0.2. What survives is what clears it by a wide margin -- `nobloom` 7.7, `nocells` 3.8, and 09-05's two bloom levers at -2.4 and -4.4, whose vsync ladders moved by whole rungs as well.

WHAT IT DOES NOT OVERTURN. The demand gate (`hasReflectiveInstance`) is still correct and still worth having for the GAME, where `probeCenter` IS set and a cube face renders every other frame for a car that may not be on screen. And the cumulus-bake fix (9/06) stands on its own code argument -- an unconditional per-frame 256-squared two-fbm pass now runs on travel -- rather than on its 1.8 ms arm, which this row puts inside the noise.

MGA-LX3 / ARM Bifrost @ DPR 2, pak `19:23 28-08-2026` ASTC over `los-santos-centre`, app `7ffd681+` (the stamp is the last COMMIT and a prebuilt archive is always built before its own commit, so it always reads one behind with a `+`; the gate was confirmed present by grepping `hasReflectiveInstance` out of the served bundle rather than by trusting the stamp). Board EMPTY, `?surface=720x640` pinned on every window, `surface.ablated` read back before any number was kept.
route: the sweep's own: settle [1500,-1500] h200 pitch -1.3 yaw pi, the rect's four corners warmed, back to the settle pose, reading A, then ten legs, reading B
howDerived: per window: delta of frame.dtHistogramMs between the post-warmup reading and the post-route reading; moving = every bin below the 100 ms tail; vsyncLadder = each moving bin rounded to the nearest 1/60 s interval; the reading is the MEAN, since p50 saturates on the 16.7 ms floor

whyThisIsANullArm.probeCenterIsNeverSet: grep over the repo: `engine.probeCenter` is assigned in apps/web/src/ui/engine-canvas-host.tsx and apps/engine-lab/src/main.ts, and set to null in apps/viewer. apps/dispatch never touches it, so it holds its declared `null`
whyThisIsANullArm.soTheGateNeverMattered: scheduleProbe's first condition is `!probeCenter`, which is true on every frame of every console capture. The 2026-09-05 demand gate (`hasReflectiveInstance`) is a THIRD condition behind it and can only fire on a surface that reached it
whyThisIsANullArm.whatTheArmActuallyRemoves: `?ablate=probe` returns one line earlier than the gate does: it skips `frameData[91] = 0` and `this.timers.probeSkipped()`. One store into a reused Float32Array and two field writes. Index 91 holds 0 either way, so the two arms upload an identical frame uniform and draw an identical picture
whyThisIsANullArm.readFromTheShippedBundle: scheduleProbe(e){if(!this.ablation.probe)return;let t=this.probeCenter;if(!t||this.environment.reflectionStrength<=0||!this.hasReflectiveInstance()){e[91]=0,this.timers.probeSkipped();return}...} -- the served asset, not the source

windows.opened: launch (reused:false), after two 60 s map_open timeouts that may each have left a tab
navigated (the attached tab steered itself from noprobe)
windows.why: THE WINDOW THAT BROKE THE STORY. Flights 1-3 read field 20.17 / noprobe 18.40 / field 20.58 and looked like a bracketed, thermally-controlled 2 ms effect. This is a `field` window at 18.11 -- inside the noprobe pair -- so the split was never by arm

spread.reading: one frame, five windows, 2.47 ms of spread. The instrument cannot resolve anything smaller than that on this device and this route

whatMovedWithTheReading.notThermal: the windows are interleaved in time and the slowest and fastest `field` windows bracket both `noprobe` windows, so a monotonic drift cannot produce this order
whatMovedWithTheReading.notTheSkipRatio: flight 3 (field, 60.5 % drawn) and flight 4 (noprobe, 62.2 % drawn) are within 2 points of each other and 2.45 ms apart
whatMovedWithTheReading.notTheWorld: all five windows report 96 draws, 241 863 triangles, 64.539 MB resident and 29 cell creates
whatMovedWithTheReading.theOneCandidateLEFT: how many console tabs the browser was holding. The panel talks to whichever is in front, a genuine launch makes a second console, and two share one GPU. Flight 1 booted in 589 ms against ~430 for the rest, and after flight 5 the panel answered from the tab flight 3 had booted -- so more than one was alive. It is a candidate rather than a finding: nothing in a capture says how many tabs exist, which is the gap this row leaves open

owed.conditions: no row in this folder records the battery level, the charging state or the die temperature, this one included
owed.tabCount: nothing in the report says how many console tabs the browser holds, and this row's one surviving explanation for its own spread is exactly that. A capture that cannot count its own competitors cannot bound its own noise
owed.probeVisibility: the report has no field saying whether the probe rendered a face. It has `frame:probe` (0 here, but 0 also when the span is simply not detailed) and nothing else, which is why 1.6 ms could be attributed for a day to a pass that has never run on this surface

verdict.theDebtIsClosed: the handoff asked for the difference between the ablation's 1.6 ms and what the fix removed. The difference is the whole 1.6 ms: the arm was never measuring the probe, and the fix had nothing to remove here
verdict.theInstrumentIsDemoted: ablation resolution on this device is ~2.5 ms, not the ~0.5 ms `render/ablation.ts` claims. Arms under it: noprobe 1.6, nocloud 1.8, noskylut 1.0, bloom4 0.2 -- none may be cited as a cost. Arms over it: nobloom 7.7, nocells 3.8, bloomrg11 -2.4, bloomhalf -4.4
verdict.andTheLadderIsTheBetTERREADING: the vsync ladder moved by whole rungs for the levers that survived (rung 1: 67 -> 80 -> 91 %) and moves inside 74-86 % for a null arm. It is noisy too, but it is the column that separated the real levers from this one
